_generation_notes.purpose: Nonstop destinations from Tallinn (TLL) and Riga (RIX), with flight duration and seasonal-route info, used by enrich_flights.py to populate flightTLL/flightRIX on each show.
_generation_notes.precedence_rule: On conflict, Wikipedia's Regular/Seasonal classification for a route is authoritative for the `seasonal` boolean (Wikipedia's airport destination tables are maintained and don't show the false-seasonal artifacts flightconnections.com's data can have). flightconnections.com is used only for `duration_minutes` (reliable, stable) and, when both sources agree a route is seasonal, for the specific `seasonal_months` range.
_generation_notes.why_flightconnections_seasonal_flag_is_n: flightconnections.com's per-destination `mths` bitmask appears to reflect whatever schedule window is currently loaded in their system rather than a route's true recurring season — e.g. it showed Tallinn-Dublin as seasonal (Dec-Aug) despite Wikipedia confirming Ryanair's TLL-Dublin route is year-round. Do not trust its seasonal boolean standalone.

flightconnections_api_technique.description: flightconnections.com renders as a JS map with no accessible destination list, but the underlying data loads from a JSON endpoint visible in the network tab.
flightconnections_api_technique.how_to_find_airport_id: Navigate to https://www.flightconnections.com/flights-from-<city>-<iata> in a real browser, open network requests, look for the rtNNN.json call.

response_shape.lst: array of [IATA, city, countryCode, countryName, durationMinutes(string), distanceKm(string), classCode] for each nonstop destination
response_shape.mths: array of 12-bit integer bitmasks, one per destination PLUS a leading 0 for the origin itself (so mths[1:] aligns with lst[0:]); 4095 = all 12 bits set = year-round; any other non-zero value = seasonal with only some months' bits set

month_bit_decoding.formula: for bit index i in 0..11: calendar_month = (BIT0_MONTH + i) % 12, where BIT0_MONTH = 2 (March, 0-indexed Jan=0)
month_bit_decoding.calibration_evidence: Verified against two Wikipedia-confirmed exact route-start dates: Riga–Kuusamo 'begins 11 December 2026' decodes to Dec–Mar under this formula (December included, consistent with a Dec-11 start); Riga–Turin 'begins 30 January 2027' decodes to Dec–Feb (January included). This is empirical calibration, not from official documentation — re-verify if the site's data format changes.
month_bit_decoding.caveat: Even with correct bit decoding, treat flightconnections' seasonal date ranges as approximate hints only, per precedence_rule above — they can reflect data-loading gaps rather than true seasonality.

_generation_notes.city_normalization: Both sources' destination names are normalized by stripping airport disambiguation (e.g. 'Rome–Fiumicino' / 'Rome (Fiumicino)' → 'Rome', 'London–Gatwick' / 'London Gatwick' → 'London') so they key consistently and match the plain city names Ticketmaster returns for venues.
_generation_notes.carrier_field: The optional `carriers` field (list of {name, iata}) is sourced only from the Wikipedia tables — flightconnections.com's rtNNN.json data has no per-route airline attribution (it only gives a separate summary of each airline's total destination count, not mapped to specific cities). Only present when direct is true. The name→IATA mapping is maintained by hand in the script that generates this field (see restructure/build script history); a carrier name with no known IATA code is simply omitted from the list rather than guessed. Known IATA codes as of this generation: {"airBaltic": "BT", "Ryanair": "FR", "Wizz Air": "W6", "LOT Polish Airlines": "LO", "Lufthansa": "LH", "Finnair": "AY", "Scandinavian Airlines": "SK", "Turkish Airlines": "TK", "Swiss International Air Lines": "LX", "Eurowings": "EW", "Jet2.com": "LS", "Norwegian Air Shuttle": "DY", "Aegean Airlines": "A3", "NyxAir": "OJ", "Pegasus Airlines": "PC", "SunExpress": "XQ", "Transavia": "HV", "flydubai": "FZ", "Uzbekistan Airways": "HY", "SkyUp Airlines": "PQ", "Air Montenegro": "4O", "FlyOne": "5F", "Freebird Airlines": "FH"}. Carriers seen in the Wikipedia data with no mapped code (logo omitted): Corendon Airlines, Heston Airlines, Mavi Gök Airlines, Skyline Express.
_generation_notes.known_naming_mismatches_between_sources: The two sources sometimes name the same airport differently, which caused duplicate city entries in an earlier version of this file (fixed once, watch for it on refresh): Wikipedia's 'Kraków'/'Reykjavík'/'Zürich' (with diacritics) vs flightconnections' 'Krakow'/'Reykjavik'/'Zurich' (ASCII); Wikipedia's 'Leeds/Bradford' vs flightconnections' 'Leeds / Bradford' (spacing); Wikipedia's 'Sharm el-Sheikh' vs flightconnections' 'Sharm El Sheikh' (case); Wikipedia's 'East Midlands' vs flightconnections' 'Nottingham' for the same airport (IATA EMA); Wikipedia's 'Cologne/Bonn' vs flightconnections' 'Cologne'. When merging carrier data in from Wikipedia, check for near-duplicate keys (accent/case/punctuation-insensitive match) before assuming a city has no entry yet.
_generation_notes.how_to_refresh: Re-fetch the two Wikipedia pages' 'Airlines and destinations' tables, and re-fetch both rtNNN.json endpoints (ids above, or re-derive via network tab if flightconnections changes airport IDs), then re-run the precedence_rule merge above, including the per-airline city mapping for the carrier field. Update `gathered_on` to the new date.
